_about: ECONOMY [tape income against armour wear] (rule 271, Paolo 10/26: 'there's not enough duct tape repaired tool shit like to be able to be bought or like loot in the world so like it feels like when my armor runs out like it's my runs over'). Where TAPE comes from besides the stall (the stall's shelf is records/target/bb/stall_prices.json tape_shelf): the loot (the men he beats carry it), the Scavenger (Battle Brothers' own), and his salvage (scrap broken down at camp). RUN FOUR's loot reads loot_tape, CAMP's salvage reads salvage, CAMP TWO's Scavenger reads scavenger. TUNING owns moving any number (the one table, section R). Measured by tools/bohemia_economy_tape_income.js, held by gates/no_run_ends_for_tape_gate.js. Record: records/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_DAY_84_NO_RUN_ENDS_FOR_TAPE_10_26_26.md. A 'quote' is its page's own words.

per_won_fight.unit: rolls of tape a won fight leaves, whatever the kills and the wrecked pieces; a lost or fled fight none
per_won_fight.source: VAMILY rule 284(a), Paolo 10/26: 'make it so I get one duct tape or something like that as a baseline'
per_won_fight.why: his baseline: the rest of a run's tape is bought (every stall, a battery a roll, 265) and mended for batteries (277), Battle Brothers' way (bb_all/2014: tools come from the market). It moves only in TUNING's one table, on a measurement of the live game, never above three a fight without his word (284(e)).

per_kill.unit: rolls in a dead man's kit, rolled even between the two (a mean of 2.5)
per_kill.why: rule 284(b), Paolo 10/26: 'you're about to crash my economy... I'm winning way too much duct tape after each fight': the kills give no tape; a won fight gives its one roll (per_won_fight). Was [2, 3] (rule 271(a)); one road fight took 40 to 53 on the live demo.

_was.why: rule 271(a), his: 'the men he beats carry tape in their kit... scaled to the kills'. Two or three rolls is what anybody in the crash carries to fix anything. Measured on rolled months at five fights a day with the shelf refilled daily: the loot alone returns about all a new crew's fights break (1.13) and nine tenths of twelve men's; with the home stall at the fair price a new crew has 1.6 to 1.7 times what it breaks and twelve men 1.15 (a camp) to 1.34 (a fortress). At a roll or two (1.5) twelve men had 0.81 at a camp

only_the_dead.why: Battle Brothers loots only the men killed by the player; the fled keep their kit

bb.why: Battle Brothers loots tools but its page gives no amount; ours is the number above

tape_of_destroyed_armour.unit: rolls for each point of top durability of every enemy piece destroyed in the fight
tape_of_destroyed_armour.quote: the number of tools recovered is equal to 0.5-1% of maximum durability of destroyed enemy armor

scavenger.why: rule 270(a): Battle Brothers' Scavenger in our skin (a woman with a shopping bag who walks the battlefield); her numbers are Battle Brothers' own

tape_per_scrap.unit: rolls of tape for every wrecked piece the loot finds (what loot.json counts as scrap)
tape_per_scrap.source: VAMILY rule 276(a): 'Scrap IS tape: the word goes; the loot counts it as tape with the tape icon, straight into the company's tape; old saves' scrap converts'
tape_per_scrap.why: rule 284(b): a wrecked piece adds no tape past the fight's one (amends 276(a)); was 2. The old-save scrap conversion reads this and so converts nothing more (284(f)); tape already in a save stays.

_was.why: his 276 (scrap is tape) on his 271(a) (scrap armour broken down into tape): every piece worn under the drop line comes home as two rolls of straps and plate, twice what Battle Brothers' Scavenger finds on a 100-point piece (bb_all/1972: up to 1 percent of its top), because his men strip it by hand. An old save's scrap converts at the same two. No camp hour: 276 puts it straight into the tape

salvage._was: Day 84 first had salvage at camp, an hour a scrap; his rule 276 (the same hour) made scrap tape straight from the loot, so the hour is gone

pace.source: VAMILY rule 264(f): 'ours runs about 5'; TUNING measured 4.6 game hours between fights (264(g))
pace.why: the measure is at the busiest the map allows, so a slower player is only better off (the shelf restocks by the day, the loot by the fight)

tape_share_max.unit: of what a new crew's fights pay, spent on tape at the map's pace
tape_share_max.source: ECONOMY Day 85 s2 (rule 284(g): the bar is the one roll plus the stall plus the smith, against what a fight pays)
tape_share_max.why: a third: a crew of three that spends a third of its pay keeping its armour up still has the rest for food, hires and gear; measured today a fifth to a quarter. Replaces 271(b)'s 'had 1.1 times what it breaks' (Day 84), which counted loot his 284 took away
